text:
**Best pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W (3× USB-C + 1× USB-A).** TechWise ranks it best overall in two separate roundups. Either of the first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone, which covers most laptops. A laptop plus one more device splits about 65W/30W, and with all four ports in use it splits 45W/30W/10.5W. It weighs 8.3 oz, the heaviest of the group, and no cable is included. Sources list it as 3 USB-C + 1 USB-A, though one roundup describes it as four USB-C, so check the listing before buying. Reviews: [TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) (the "Check price on Amazon" button is there), [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger).

**Other good options**
- **Anker Prime 67W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A):** Best if you want small and light (4.78 oz). Either USB-C port gives the full 67W alone, and it holds about 64.5W with all three ports in use. It's a good fit for one laptop, one phone and one accessory. [VoyageHacks review](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/) | [TechWise review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026)
- **Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A):** Best if one demanding laptop is your priority. It has only three ports, and power is still shared. [TechWise review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A), 2-pack, $49.99** (list $59.99, verified Oct 21, 2026): [Buy at Baseus via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u). This is an affiliate link. With two or three devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W. That's fine for a MacBook Air but slow for a 65W laptop. It comes with an 18–24 month warranty and a 7-day return window. [Product page](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u)
- **Baseus GaN6 100W (4 ports, two of them USB-A):** A value 100W option that includes a 3.3 ft extension cord. [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)

**Traveling abroad?** The chargers above have US-style folding prongs, so you'd need a separate plug adapter, not a voltage converter. If you'd rather have one device, Android Central's [travel adapter roundup](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel) lists:
- Epicka TA-105 Max 75W: 3× USB-C + 2× USB-A, with swappable plugs.
- UGREEN 65W Nexode travel adapter: 2× USB-C + 1× USB-A.

**Tips**
- For a laptop, aim for 65W or more, and plug it into the charger's top USB-C port first.
- For chargers over 60W, use a 5A-rated cable. Without one, the cable limits your charging speed.

If you tell me which laptop and phone you're bringing, I can narrow this to one pick.
